oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable in content.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token/id_token claim sets as overbroad issuance by themselves.

oidc_jwt.description: Session-based authentication using cookies bypasses scope checking for MCP and grants full tool access.
oidc_jwt.note: Use bearer tokens for scope tests; cookie-auth success is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
oidc_jwt.note: Admin access to tagged applications is expected and should not be reported as authorization escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documentation describes standard OAuth/JWT token issuance and introspection but does not document jti replay tracking for bearer JWTs.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same stateless bearer JWT is not by itself evidence of a replay flaw under RFC 7519 expectations.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers with the suffix -org-<organizationName>.
oidc_jwt.note: Organization suffixes on client IDs are expected and should not be treated as identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Submitting authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a temporary guest account instead of completing a normal code exchange.
oidc_jwt.note: This is a documented extension; resulting guest_<uuid> usernames are expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
oidc_jwt.note: Some cross-login identity merges are configured behavior, not necessarily a principal-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: For SAML providers, if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email and then NameID.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity names differing from the original upstream username may be expected due to documented fallback mapping.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and states they can be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claim sets as token confusion by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only contains claims allowed by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email fields in userinfo are expected when those scopes were not requested.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect/resource-binding tests, if the authorization request includes the RFC 8707 resource parameter, the token request MUST include the same resource value exactly. Casdoor documentation states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; mismatches can fail the flow for by-design reasons rather than indicating a security bug.

For PKCE-based authorization code tests, when code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are used at /login/oauth/authorize, the token request to /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST include the original code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret missing/incorrect code_verifier failures as broader auth bugs.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Casdoor-issued tokens, include a CONTROL flow that obtains a valid token first, then call /api/userinfo or /api/login/oauth/introspect with that token. Without a control, a failed attack token cannot be distinguished from broken application configuration, bad client credentials, or redirect/resource mismatch.

Refresh token lifetime has sentinel semantics: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states default 0 hours for refresh token expiration; do not assume 0 means immediate expiry without verifying application behavior. Treat 0 as a special configured/default value, not a generic numeric literal.

Code resend timeout has sentinel semantics: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown instead.

For I2 logout/freshness tests, Casdoor invalidates tokens on SSO logout by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. A token failing after logout is by design and should not be treated as anomalous replay protection beyond documented logout invalidation.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, when scope is omitted in token exchange, Casdoor inherits the subject token's scope by design. To test scope narrowing or escalation, explicitly send scope in the token exchange request; otherwise inherited scopes can mask the intended condition.

For I5 token_exchange tests, Casdoor accepts subject_token_type values urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Use the correct declared subject_token_type for the token under test; mismatches can cause by-design rejection unrelated to audience or scope binding.

For I5 audience-binding tests, when the authorization request includes resource, Casdoor sets the resulting access token aud claim to that resource URI instead of the client ID. Tests that expect aud=client_id must omit resource; tests that validate audience enforcement should compare against the exact resource URI when resource is used.

For I4 cross-org/shared-app tests, shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. Do not treat organization-specific client IDs for a shared application as identity confusion; this suffixing is by design.

For I4 username/case-collision tests, if organization setting isUsernameLowered is enabled, usernames are converted to lowercase by configuration. Case-folding collisions under that setting are by-design normalization, not necessarily a broker identity-binding flaw.

For I4 account-linking tests with external OAuth/OIDC providers, Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). Cross-user merges under those configured linking rules may be by design; verify whether automatic account linking is enabled before flagging identity collapse.

For I4 provider-specific username mapping tests, some OAuth providers intentionally map usernames from provider-specific identifiers rather than a generic sub/email. Examples documented: Lark chooses UserId, then UnionId, then OpenId; DingTalk uses unionid; Baidu uses a masked username. Do not assume the granted username will equal the upstream email or a generic claim across all providers.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or application APIs, session-based authentication via browser cookies bypasses scope checking and grants full access to MCP tools by design. Use Bearer access tokens, not session cookies, when testing scope enforcement.

For I5 custom-scope tests, custom scopes are available only for applications with category Agent. Default applications expose only standard OAuth/OIDC scopes. Do not attempt custom-scope authorization tests on Default-category applications.

For I5 token parsing tests, Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same and contain the same JWT payload. Treat differences between access_token and id_token claims as non-applicable on this platform; session_token for API use should still be access_token.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and general authorization-code tests, the redirect_uri used at /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST match exactly. Casdoor documentation explicitly requires the same redirect URI and treats callback URL matching as exact application configuration.

For I5 audience/resource binding tests, when using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter MUST be included consistently in BOTH the authorization request and the token request, and the value must match exactly. Otherwise failures may be due to setup mismatch rather than audience enforcement.

For I3 PKCE tests, if PKCE is enabled for the application or provider flow, the token request MUST include code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret failures from missing code_verifier as identity or authorization bugs.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a CONTROL login with a known-good token or authorization flow in the same application configuration. A failed token request can also be caused by disabled grant types, bad redirect URI, missing PKCE verifier, or wrong client credentials.

Cookie/session lifetime has sentinel semantics: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiration. Do not use 0 in session-freshness tests expecting instant expiry.

Casdoor token exchange allows subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token. For I5 token-exchange audience/scope tests, vary subject_token_type explicitly because access_token and id_token are both accepted token classes and may exercise different validation paths.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation says omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing. Therefore the fuzzer MUST request an explicitly broader scope than the original when testing escalation, and compare returned scope/claims against the original authorization.

For I5 audience tests, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI when resource is supplied; otherwise audience behavior may default to the client ID. The fuzzer MUST distinguish these two modes and not treat client_id audience as a resource-binding failure.

Casdoor applications can be shared across organizations by appending -org-<organizationName> to client_id or application name. For cross-organization and cross-tenant tests, the fuzzer MUST treat suffixed shared-app client IDs as distinct tenant contexts, not as accidental identity collisions.

Application tag enforcement restricts sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, but admins and global admins are exempt. Do NOT use admin accounts for I5 authorization-binding tests involving application tags, or results will appear over-permissive by design.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for OAuth logins by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For I4 cross-user-collision and case-confusion tests, use fresh users and avoid overlapping email/phone/username values unless the test specifically targets linking behavior; otherwise identity merges may be by design.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation states OAuth account linking can occur by username case-insensitively. Therefore usernames differing only by case may intentionally merge. Use distinct non-case-equivalent identifiers when testing unintended collisions.

For I4 username mapping tests with Lark and DingTalk, Casdoor derives usernames from provider-specific stable identifiers (Lark: UserId then UnionId then OpenId; DingTalk: unionid). Do not compare downstream username directly to arbitrary upstream display fields for these providers; compare against the documented identifier source.

For I4 SAML-vs-OIDC or external-provider merge tests, SAML provider overview states that if username mapping is absent, Casdoor falls back to email, then NameID. This can intentionally merge identities sharing email. Distinguish configured fallback behavior from unintended principal collapse.

Casdoor user IDs can be represented as either <organization>/<username> or just <username> for single-organization applications, while tokens use a stable UUID sub. For I4 verification, compare stable identifiers carefully and do not flag organization-prefix formatting differences as collisions.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or API consumers, session-based authentication bypasses scope checking and grants full access to all tools. The fuzzer MUST use Bearer access tokens, not browser session cookies, when testing scope enforcement.

For I5 token format and claim-shape tests, token format affects claim encoding. In JWT/JWT-Empty/JWT-Custom, address is a raw string array; only JWT-Standard emits OIDC-compliant address object. Do not treat address-shape differences as authorization bugs unless token format is controlled.

For I5 claim type tests, JWT-Custom token attributes have explicit Array vs String typing. When testing type confusion on roles/groups/permissions-like claims, configure the token attribute type intentionally; otherwise array-vs-string differences may be caused by token-format configuration rather than validation flaws.

For RFC 8707 audience-binding tests (I5), if start_oidc_auth includes resource, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the identical resource value. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client ID, and the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, token_exchange SHOULD request a scope that is a strict subset of the subject token scope for the control case. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope; requesting broader scope may be rejected or may reflect requested expansion rather than a broker bug.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style freshness tests on OAuth/OIDC flows, include a control authorization_code or password-grant login using a known-good token setup in the same test campaign. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from bad client/app configuration, redirect URI mismatch, or disabled grant type.

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states default 0 hours is a configured default value, not evidence that refresh is disabled by protocol. Never assume 0 means immediate expiry without verifying the application setting semantics in the target instance.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Do not build timing assertions that interpret 0 as no wait.
Cookie/session lifetime has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours of 0 means use the default lifetime, not immediate expiration. Do not use 0 when testing session freshness or logout timing.

For I3 config-change tests involving application settings, new logins after an admin changes grant types, redirect URIs, token format, scopes, or exclusive sign-in behavior are expected to follow the updated configuration. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests across the config change, not treat the admin change itself as a bug.

For I4 multi-organization tests, Casdoor user identity is organization-scoped and commonly represented as <organization>/<username>; the same username in different organizations is expected to be distinct. Do not flag cross-organization namespace prefixes as identity collisions by themselves.

For I4 shared-application tests, shared applications require appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. If the suffix is omitted, authentication may target the wrong organization context and produce misleading identity-binding results.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or OAuth-protected APIs, session/cookie authentication bypasses scope checking for MCP while bearer access tokens enforce scopes. Use bearer access tokens, not browser session auth, when testing whether granted permissions exceed requested scopes.

For I5 audience tests using introspection, remember that Casdoor may issue access tokens with aud equal to the resource URI when the resource parameter is used, otherwise aud may be the client ID. The oracle must compare against the request mode used in the test.

For PKCE-related OIDC flow tests, when PKCE is enabled the token request should include code_verifier; client_secret becomes optional but if provided it must be correct. Missing or wrong code_verifier/client_secret can cause expected flow rejection unrelated to identity invariants.
